newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2959 on Tuesday from Monday's 8.2964 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai, boosted by China's growing foreign trade surplus, traders said.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2965.
Dealers said news of the trade surplus had significantly strengthened pro-yuan sentiment.
The official Xinhua news agency said China posted a trade surplus of $6.71 billion in the first three months of this year, up 25.7 percent year-on-year.
The yuan opened lower at 8.2967 and hit an intraday low of 8.2970 early in the session. It then rose solidly up towards the close, hitting a high of 8.2946.
Trading was active with most business done in a narrow range of 8.2960 and 8.2965, traders said.
One dealer said that a high trade surplus figure had been expected, which initially limited the impact on the market.
"But the high growth rate started to attract yuan buying soon after the opening, and the currency was pushed up as a result," he added.
A second dealer said the People Bank of China, the central bank, was seen depressing the yuan at about 8.2950 to halt the uptrend.
"As a result of the intervention, the yuan failed to breach that resistance level today," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to stick around 8.2965 on Wednesday.
The yuan closed slightly up at 6.5695 from 6.5721 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at 1.0714 from 1.0715 against the Hong Kong dollar.
